summary.text: Carolyn Wiezorek is the Democratic candidate for Iowa House of Representatives District 65 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Republican Shannon Lundgren.
A former teacher, elementary school principal and university professor of education, she also ran for the seat in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Carolyn Wiezorek was born in Dubuque, Iowa, and graduated from Wahlert High School.

She earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Iowa in 1984 and a degree from the University of Northern Iowa in 2012, and her career experience includes working as a teacher, elementary school administrator and university professor.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she and her husband, Bill, have three adult children and two grandchildren, own a small farm near Bankston and are part-owners of a sawmill in Sand Springs.

Wiezorek was the Democratic nominee for Iowa House District 65 in 2024, when she lost to incumbent Republican Shannon Lundgren, receiving 6,623 votes (35.7 percent) to Lundgren's 11,934 (64.2 percent).

In her survey, she listed three key messages: representing her community and stopping legislation she said is promoted by out-of-state interests, strengthening the economy through a progressive income tax and protections against private equity and corporate monopolies, and improving healthcare access, including reversing the privatization of Medicaid.
